title: Theodosius I's secret pact with pagan relics in 380
hook: A hidden 380 decree shows Theodosius I quietly blending pagan art into Christian worship.

beats.say: In 380, Theodosius I secretly ordered the removal of pagan statues from the Temple of Serapis, shocking Rome.
He feared the hidden cult of Mithras could rally soldiers against his Christian reforms, a threat rarely mentioned.
To neutralize it, he dispatched the elite Scholae Palatinae to seize the underground mithraic altar in the Subura.
The soldiers uncovered a bronze relief depicting the cosmic battle of Ahura Mazda, evidence of Persian influence in Rome.
Instead of destroying it, Theodosius ordered its relocation to the newly built Church of St. John, blending faiths.
beats.visual: Church of St. John interior 4th century

beats.say: This act sparked the first recorded instance of a pagan artifact being consecrated within a Christian basilica.
Contemporary letters from Bishop Ambrose describe the ceremony as a 'truce between gods,' hinting at political pragmatism.
Historians once claimed Theodosius banned all pagan worship that year, but the decree targeted only high-profile cults.
The subtle compromise kept the army's Mithraic veterans loyal, securing his victory at the Battle of the Frigidus.
Thus, 380 became the hidden turning point where Christianity learned to co-opt, not just crush, Rome's mysteries.
